theater: 柏林街壘與中部德意志邦國

battle.name: 德意志1848年革命
battle.theater: 柏林街壘與中部德意志邦國
battle.brief: 一八四八年三月十八日至十九日，柏林的國民守衛隊與工人以街壘對抗普魯士軍，國王被迫承諾言論自由與軍隊改革；三月廿九日法蘭克福國民議會在聖保羅教堂開議，萊茵民軍與普法爾茨義軍隨後北進，石勒蘇益格戰爭把普軍拉向北方。雷管步槍在街壘射擊中可靠擊發，讓守壘者在近距離內得以抵擋。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries: 交戰方是德意志邦聯各邦的政府軍與城市、鄉村起義者之間的一連串衝突。柏林方面由普魯士國王腓特烈·威廉四世主持，軍隊指揮一度交給威廉親王與阿達爾貝特親王，參謀本部與國防部的高層將領在柏林坐鎮，三月十九日軍隊撤出首都後，內政部由莫蘭滕菲爾等人接手善後。萊茵與南德方面，普魯士王國、奧地利帝國與巴伐利亞王國的聯軍奉聯邦議會之命進入巴登與普法爾茨，法國二月革命後成立的臨時政府派出的臨時軍越過萊茵河與普法爾茨義軍合流，戰事後來在維也納與匈牙利方向延續。起義方並無統一司令部：柏林的國民守衛隊與工人武裝、維也納的帝國議會與各民族代表、維也納的匈牙利與義大利軍團、法蘭克福的國民議會，以及萊茵各城的國民警衛隊、萊茵獵兵營與獅子磨坊的義軍，各按自己的議程行動。德意志邦聯的聯邦議會與聯邦軍在三月內向各省調兵，但調度慢於城市起事，聯邦軍的指揮又受制於各邦君主的意圖，這是它無法迅速平定的原因。
countriesEn: The two sides were a series of conflicts between the governments of the states of the German Confederation and the insurgents in the towns and villages. In Berlin the king was Friedrich Wilhelm IV; command of the troops passed to Prince William and Prince Adalbert, and the senior generals of the general staff and the ministry of war sat in the capital, while after the troops withdrew on 19 March the interior ministry was taken over by men such as Manteuffel. In the Rhineland and southern Germany, a league of troops from Prussia, Austria and Bavaria entered Baden and the Palatinate on the orders of the federal diet, and the provisional government created by the February revolution in France sent its troops across the Rhine to join the insurgents of the Palatinate, with the war later stretching towards Vienna and Hungary. The insurgent side had no unified command: the Berlin National Guard and the workers' armed bands, the imperial diet in Vienna with its deputies of many nations, the Hungarian and Italian legions in Vienna, the national parliament in Frankfurt, and the civic guards of the Rhineland towns, the Rhenish Jaeger corps and the volunteers of the Lion Mill all followed their own programme. The federal diet and the federal army moved troops towards the provinces during March, but the movement was slower than the risings in the cities, and the command of the federal army was tied to the wishes of the individual princes, which is why it could not restore order quickly.
people: 柏林的街壘由兩股力量推動：國民警衛隊與工人武裝。威廉親王三月十七日對營房的講話呼籲士兵維護軍紀、不要向國民開槍，反而加深了國王與軍方的裂痕；真正令軍隊退回城門與營房的是街壘的數量與抵抗的持續，國王隨即頒布特赦，承認新聞自由並答應召集國民議會與改革軍制。國民警衛隊的指揮層是工人出身的骨幹軍人與學生出身的義工的混合，前者提供了操槍與編制的經驗，後者提供了街壘的組織速度，這種混合正是柏林街壘能在一夜之間成形的原因。德國各地的民軍指揮者同樣關鍵：巴登的民軍指揮洛倫茨·布倫塔諾以整肅與紀律著稱，他率民軍越過萊茵河支援普法爾茨的義軍；普法爾茨的義軍領袖有共和派宣傳家弗洛里安·黑爾弗，以及法國臨時政府派往德意志邦聯的專員卡爾·馬蒂，後者在普法爾茨主持了與法軍的聯合行動。萊茵地區的自由派國民議會由海因里希·馮·加格爾主持，議會在五月決定組織十萬人的中央軍並派兵支援南德，但指揮權與撥款在議會、邦政府與中央權力之間始終無法統一。石勒蘇益格方面，普軍由朗格爾將軍主持對杜佩爾的圍攻而未能取勝，丹麥軍由比洛將軍指揮，戰事拖到一八四九年仍未了結。
peopleEn: The barricades of Berlin were driven by two forces: the National Guard and the armed workers. On 17 March Prince William spoke to the barracks and called on the soldiers to keep discipline and not to fire on the citizens, which deepened the rift between the king and the officer corps; what actually drove the troops back behind the gates and into their quarters was the sheer number of barricades and the way the resistance held, and the king then issued a general amnesty, conceded freedom of the press and promised a national assembly and a reform of the army. The command of the National Guard was a mixture of working men with military experience and students acting as volunteers; the first supplied the handling of weapons and the organisation of the units, the second the speed with which barricades could be built, and that mixture is why the Berlin barricades took shape within a single night. The commanders of the popular militias were no less important: the Baden militia under Lorenz Brentano was noted for its order and discipline, and he led it across the Rhine to support the insurgents of the Palatinate; the leaders of the Palatinate rising included the republican propagandist Florian Hecker and Karl Mathy, the commissioner sent by the French provisional government to the German Confederation, who organised the joint action with the French troops in the Palatinate. The liberal national parliament of the Rhineland was presided over by Heinrich von Gagern; in May it decided to raise a central army of a hundred thousand men and to send troops to the south, but command and money never came into agreement between the parliament, the state governments and the central power. On the Schleswig front the siege of Düppel was directed by General Wrangel and failed, while the Danish defence was led by General Bülow, and the war was still unsettled in 1849.
kits: 本卡雷管步槍在一八四八年的德意志，意義在於它是雷管化浪潮中的法式標本：底火在潮濕與陰雨裡仍能擊發，射程較火繩槍拉長，射擊精度提高，代價是隊形在有效射程之外難以維持。普魯士陸軍的制式步槍是一八三九年式德勒塞針式雷管槍，彈藥為紙包，精度極高但後膛結構易髒且產量有限；柏林的國民警衛隊拿到的多是普軍淘汰下來的舊式火繩步槍與少量一八四二年式雷管步槍，軍械庫的存量在十八日之後成為守壘者最急需的東西。開進普法爾茨的巴登民軍與萊茵義軍攜帶的是各邦配發的雷管火槍與獵槍，萊茵獵兵營與獅子磨坊的志願兵多為手工業者出身，槍械自備、口徑雜亂，彈藥靠城鎮商會募給。砲兵方面，參與街壘戰的多是守壘者臨時徵用的舊式攻城砲與臼砲，而普軍在撤出柏林後依賴鐵路與營屬砲推進到邦國邊境，以優勢砲火與齊射面對缺乏野砲的義軍。與此同時，國民警衛隊制度在三月之後被廣泛質疑：國民要求解散常備軍、由國民警衛隊武裝國家，這一要求在同年十月之後與軍方及國王的聯盟正面衝突，結果是民兵被解除武裝。
kitsEn: In Germany in 1848 the percussion rifle on this card mattered as a French specimen of the wave of percussion: the priming composition fired in damp and rainy weather, the range was longer than that of the flint musket and the accuracy better, and the price was that formations could not be held together beyond effective range. The standard musket of the Prussian army was the Dreyse needle gun of 1839, using paper cartridges, extremely accurate but prone to fouling and produced in limited numbers; what the Berlin National Guard received was mostly older flint muskets and a few percussion muskets of the 1842 model, and after the eighteenth the contents of the arsenals were the thing the defenders most needed. The Baden militia that marched into the Palatinate and the Rhineland insurgents carried the percussion guns and hunting pieces issued by their own states, while the Rhenish Jaeger corps and the volunteers of the Lion Mill were largely artisans who brought their own weapons of mixed calibre and bought their ammunition with money collected by the town merchants. On the artillery side the barricades were usually defended by old siege pieces and mortars requisitioned on the spot, while the Prussians, after leaving Berlin, relied on the railways and on brigade guns to press towards the borders of the states, meeting insurgents who had no field artillery at all with concentrated gun fire and massed volleys. At the same time the institution of the civic militia was widely questioned after March: the citizens demanded the disbandment of the standing army and the arming of the state by the National Guard, and that demand came into open collision with the alliance of the officers and the king later in the same year. The result was that the militias were disarmed.
tactics: 三月的德意志起事提供了兩種截然不同的戰術樣本。柏林的街壘戰是短促而密集的：民眾用磚石、推車與鐵柵封住交叉路口，守壘者以房屋窗口與屋頂射擊孔構成多層交叉火力，使普軍的密集射擊線在狹窄街道裡失去縱深，砲兵一旦失去射界便無從施展；軍隊最終選擇撤出首都而不是逐街硬攻。萊茵與南德的起義則更多依賴機動：民軍以營為單位沿主要道路推進，與普法爾茨的義軍在邊境會合，再一度進軍巴伐利亞，並在維也納方向與匈牙利、義大利的武裝合流，試圖把德意志的革命延伸到多民族帝國。這種機動同樣暴露弱點：隊伍分散、彈藥與糧秣靠徵發，沒有統一的補給線，一遇到帝國與邦國聯軍的縱隊與砲兵即失去主動。德意志各邦的國民警衛隊在編制上模仿普軍，用連營制與小型砲兵連，紀律比柏林的工人武裝好，卻同樣缺砲、缺騎兵、缺彈藥生產。整體看，這一年的德意志戰爭是一次街壘加民軍對縱隊加營屬砲的總體較量。
tacticsEn: The risings of March in Germany offered two very different tactical models. The fighting in the Berlin barricades was short and dense: the people blocked the intersections with bricks, carts and iron railings, and the defenders built crossfire from the windows and roof openings of the houses, so that the dense lines of Prussian fire lost their depth in the narrow streets and the artillery had nothing to shoot at once its field of fire was lost; the troops finally chose to leave the capital rather than fight street by street. The risings in the Rhineland and the south depended far more on movement: militias advanced by battalion along the main roads, joined the insurgents of the Palatinate at the frontier, marched into Bavaria again and linked up with the Hungarian and Italian armed groups in the direction of Vienna, trying to carry the German revolution into a multinational empire. That mobility exposed its own weakness: the columns were dispersed, ammunition and food were taken by requisition, and there was no unified line of supply, so the first serious meeting with the columns and artillery of the imperial and state alliance cost them the initiative at once. The civic guards of the German states imitated the Prussian organisation in battalion and company, with small artillery sections, and their discipline was better than that of the Berlin workers, but they lacked guns, cavalry and any production of ammunition in the same way. Taken as a whole, the German war of that year was a general trial of barricades and militia against columns and brigade guns.
data: 可核對的時間與數字如下。柏林街壘戰集中於一八四八年三月十八日至十九日；三月廿八日普魯士政府同意召開國民議會，三月廿九日法蘭克福國民議會在聖保羅教堂開幕，四月十八日至二十二日德意志各邦的選舉產生了全國議會，議會在五月決定組建中央權力與十萬人的帝國軍。五月聯邦議會在紐倫堡通過要求各邦交出國民警衛隊武裝的決議，聯邦軍隨即在普法爾茨實行封鎖並向巴登施壓。石勒蘇益格戰爭自一八四八年二月延續：普軍三月二十日在伊德斯科夫一度敗績，四月對杜佩爾的圍攻未果，八月廿六日簽訂馬爾默停戰協議。柏林街壘的傷亡數字各方統計出入甚大，不宜引用；可確定的數字是三月十八日一夜之間柏林的街壘達到數十道，軍隊在十八日夜撤出中央城區，國民警衛隊在數日內組成了數千人的武裝，聯邦議會五月計畫的帝國軍則是十萬人。
dataEn: The dates and figures that can be checked run as follows. The fighting in the Berlin barricades was concentrated on 18 and 19 March 1848; on 28 March the Prussian government agreed to summon a national assembly, and on 29 March the national parliament opened in St Paul's Church at Frankfurt; the elections in the German states from 18 to 22 April produced a national assembly, and in May that assembly decided to create a central power and an imperial army of a hundred thousand men. In May the federal diet passed the resolution at Nuremberg requiring the states to hand over the arms of the civic militias, and the federal army then blockaded the Palatinate and pressed on Baden. The war in Schleswig ran from February 1848: the Prussians suffered a reverse at Idskov on 20 March, their siege of Düppel in April failed, and the armistice of Malmö was signed on 26 August. Casualty figures for the Berlin barricades vary widely between sources and are better not quoted; what is certain is that several dozen barricades existed in Berlin after a single night on 18 March, that the troops withdrew from the central city that night, that the National Guard organised a force of several thousand within days, and that the imperial army planned by the federal diet in May was to number a hundred thousand men.
cause: 起因是德意志邦聯體制本身的失效。一八一五年維也納會議把德意志置於聯邦議會與三十四個邦國之下，聯邦議會由奧地利主持並握有維也納的駐軍權，這套安排在政治上把奧地利與德意志的民族要求綁在一起，卻既無中央軍，也無統一的行政。隨著工業化推進，萊茵地區的資產者與工匠要求一部全德憲章、統一的關稅與司法，而書刊檢查制度、封建特權、各邦的郵政與關稅障礙仍橫在面前，一八四四年的關稅同盟雖已拆除經濟壁壘，政治壁壘卻原封不動。飢荒與一八四六至四七年的商業危機把職業貧民推到街道上，讓起義多了一份社會動因。直接引爆點是消息傳播的速度：二月二十四日巴黎的消息於三月一日前後抵達萊茵與柏林，柏林的群眾集會迅速升級，十八日開始築起街壘。同樣在三月，維也納、威尼斯、米蘭與布達佩斯相繼發生革命，整個中歐像被同一根引線串起，德意志各邦的議會與城市議會幾乎在同一個月內被要求召開國民議會、廢除出版檢查、改革軍制。德意志的特殊性在於：起事並不反對德意志民族本身，而是在爭取以德意志民族的名義重建邦聯，於是革命議會同時要在對外與對內兩條戰線上作戰，這種雙重性使它的每一次軍事行動都帶著政治負擔。
causeEn: The cause was the failure of the German Confederation system itself. The Congress of Vienna in 1815 placed Germany under a federal diet and thirty-four states, with the diet presided over by Austria and the right to garrison Vienna; politically this tied Austria to German national demands, while providing neither a central army nor a central administration. As industrialisation advanced, the asset owners and craftsmen of the Rhineland wanted a general German constitution, uniform tariffs and a common judiciary, while censorship, feudal privileges and the postal and tariff barriers of the individual states still stood in the way; the customs union of 1844 had removed the economic barriers but left the political ones untouched. Famine and the commercial crisis of 1846 and 1847 pushed the working poor into the streets and gave the rising a social motive as well. The immediate trigger was the speed with which news travelled: the news of Paris on 24 February reached the Rhineland and Berlin around 1 March, the meetings in Berlin escalated quickly, and on the eighteenth the barricades went up. In the same month Vienna, Venice, Milan and Budapest rose in turn, so that central Europe seemed lit by a single fuse, and within weeks the diets and city councils of the German states were being asked to summon national assemblies, to abolish censorship and to reform the armies. What was peculiar to Germany was that the risings did not oppose the German nation itself but sought to rebuild the Confederation in the name of that nation; the revolutionary parliament therefore had to fight on two fronts at once, and that double burden was carried by every military operation it undertook.
impact: 一八四八年的德意志革命在軍事上全面失敗，卻在制度與思想上留下長久痕跡。最直接的後果是革命陣營的分裂：議會左派要求把中央權力交給國民警衛隊並接管軍隊，軍方、邦政府與資產者的聯盟則在十月前後把國民武裝逐一解散或收編，柏林的武裝工人被資產者民兵清剿，大批流亡者前往巴黎與倫敦，馬克思與恩格斯的《共產黨宣言》正是在同年二月問世，與革命的爆發僅隔數日。制度上，法蘭克福議會於一八四九年三月通過全德憲法，五月把帝國王冠獻給腓特烈·威廉四世卻遭拒絕，此後那句從溝渠裡撈起王冠的說法便成為德意志政治中對革命君主制的固定指責；同年八月議會遷往斯圖加特，最後流亡，帝國的設想停在紙面上。軍隊的角色則被徹底扭轉：紅軍制度的存廢成為國王與議會衝突的核心，一八五〇年十一月奧爾米茨條約使普魯士在歐洲事務上重新屈居奧地利之下，同時也確定了普魯士用軍事手段主導德意志事務的方向；一八四九年普法爾茨與巴登再度起事被聯邦軍鎮壓，兩名民軍指揮官被處決，之後聯邦軍對南德的軍事接管更為直接。德國鐵路在這幾年裡的快速延伸，配合普軍以鐵路調度兵力的能力，成為一八六六與一八七〇年諸戰役的物質前提。
impactEn: The German revolution of 1848 failed militarily in every respect, yet it left durable marks on institutions and ideas. The most immediate consequence was the split inside the revolutionary camp: the left of the parliament wanted the central power handed to the National Guard and the army taken over by the citizens, while the alliance of the officers, the state governments and the property owners disbanded or absorbed the armed citizens in the months around October; the armed workers of Berlin were cleared out by the bourgeois militia, large numbers of exiles went to Paris and London, and the Communist Manifesto of Marx and Engels appeared in February of that same year, only days before the revolutions began. In institutional terms the Frankfurt parliament passed a German constitution in March 1849 and offered the imperial crown to Friedrich Wilhelm IV in May, only to be refused, after which the phrase about picking a crown out of the gutter became a fixed reproach against revolutionary monarchy in German politics; in August the parliament moved to Stuttgart and finally went into exile, and the empire remained on paper. The role of the army was turned completely inside out: the survival of the Landwehr became the core of the quarrel between the king and the parliament, and the punctation of Olmütz in November 1850 put Prussia back below Austria in European affairs while at the same time fixing the direction in which Prussia would use military power to lead German affairs. The rising in the Palatinate and Baden in 1849 was crushed by the federal army, two militia commanders were executed, and the federal presence in southern Germany afterwards became more direct. The rapid extension of the German railways in these years, together with the ability of the Prussian army to move troops along them, was the material precondition for the campaigns of 1866 and 1870.
result: 德意志革命在每一場軍事衝突中都是防守方的失敗，但失敗的同時也確定了聯邦軍的勝利方式。柏林以撤退換取國王的讓步，街壘被放棄；萊茵義軍在普法爾茨與巴登因彈藥、砲兵與後勤不足，在聯邦軍的縱隊與砲火面前解體；漢堡的國民警衛隊在九月一度頂住聯邦軍的干預，卻最終在邦國聯軍的攻擊前失去戰鬥力，而各邦的民兵在十月之後被解散或收編。戰局的關鍵轉折有兩個：聯邦軍一旦能以縱隊與營屬砲進入鄉村，義軍的游擊優勢就立刻消失；而議會與中央權力無法統一指揮與撥款，使得跨邦的義軍只能各自作戰，無法形成會戰。裝備層面的結果同樣清楚：街壘時代的勝負取決於能否及時取得火槍與彈藥，而一八四八年之後的趨勢，是把射擊精度與砲火的集中重新交回國家軍隊。雷管步槍在這一年最大的作用是示範：底火讓槍械在雨霧中可用，卻不能讓沒有砲兵、沒有鐵路、沒有統一指揮的義軍贏下一場會戰。
resultEn: In every military encounter the German revolution ended in the defeat of those who were defending, and the manner of that defeat fixed the way the federal army won. Berlin bought the concessions of the king with a withdrawal, and the barricades were given up; the insurgents of the Rhineland came apart in the Palatinate and in Baden for want of ammunition, artillery and supply when the columns and guns of the federal army came forward; the civic guard of Hamburg held off federal intervention for a time in September but lost its fighting power before the allied troops of the states, and the militias were dissolved or absorbed in the months after October. There were two turning points in the course of events: once the federal army could advance into the countryside in column with brigade guns, the advantage of insurgent raiding vanished at once; and the failure of the parliament and the central power to agree on command and money meant that the insurgents of different states could only fight separately and could never bring about a general action. The result at the level of equipment is equally plain: in the age of the barricade the outcome turned on whether arms and ammunition could be obtained in time, and the tendency after 1848 was to give accuracy in fire and the concentration of guns back to the armies of the state. The great service of the percussion rifle in that year was demonstration: the priming composition made weapons usable in rain and mist, but it could not give an army without artillery, without railways and without a unified command the victory in a set-piece battle.
